title: Dal Makhani
subtitle: Slow-cooked lentils and kidney beans in a rich, buttery tomato sauce
excerpt: Dal makhani is a Punjabi classic that earns its reputation through time. The longer the lentils simmer, the more the tomato and butter meld into a sauce that coats every grain. It is one of the great vegetarian comfort dishes, as satisfying as any slow-cooked meat.
sourceNotes: Dal makhani originated in the Punjab region and was popularised by Kundan Lal Gujral, founder of Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, in the 1940s. The original recipe used a slow overnight cook over a wood fire.

content.text: The key to great dal makhani is patience: keep the heat low and let the lentils cook until they begin to break down and thicken the sauce naturally. If the dal looks too thick at any point, add a splash of water rather than turning up the heat, which risks catching on the base.
Put the rinsed lentils in the saucepan with 1 litre of cold water. Bring to the boil, skim any foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 30 minutes until tender but not falling apart.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds, then add the onion. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, tomato puree, turmeric, coriander, and chilli flakes. Cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the tinned tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the cooked lentils with their cooking water and the drained kidney beans. Stir well and simmer for 20 minutes until the dal is thick and creamy. Add a splash of water if it catches on the base.
Stir in the double cream and garam masala. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt. Simmer for a further 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The lentils are still firm after 30 minutes
items.cause: Older dried lentils take longer to cook, and hard water can slow the process
items.fix: Continue simmering, adding water as needed, and check every 10 minutes. They will soften.

items.cause: Too much cooking water, or insufficient simmering time
items.fix: Remove the lid and increase the heat slightly to reduce the liquid. Stir frequently to stop the base catching.
